text:
Anna M: Ran an nsys trace against the continuous-batch profile on prod-sim today. Seeing ~3-4ms latency spikes every ~120ms. spikes line up with batch window boundaries. attaching timeline screenshot (link).

Raj P: Can you paste the kernel timeline snippet? suspect kernel preemption or big matmul chunks.

Anna M: here's the interesting bit from the nsys timeline:

````
0.001234s cutlass_sgemm kernel (0.98ms)
0.002250s kv_get (0.05ms)
0.003120s cutlass_sgemm (3.72ms)  <-- LONG
0.006900s layernorm_fwd (0.12ms)
0.007050s batch_dispatcher: wavejoin (0.02ms)
````

Mike L: That long cutlass run correlates with queue draining at the end of the micro-batch window. Also noticed KV cache sweeps at same offsets: kv_get latency jumps.

Lucy G: Could be two things: kernel choice (large matmul vs small tiled matmul) or kvcache eviction/rehash. Which kernel variant compiled for this model run? also what's batch_window_ms set to?

Anna M: batch_window_ms = 2.0ms on that node group. Kernel selector picks cutlass_sgemm.large for >512 tokens. But our trace shows seq_len ~128, so weird.

Raj P: maybe sequence packing causes occasional large concat leading to fallback. Do we have the dispatch logs? try `RUNTIME_DEBUG=kernel_dispatch:trace` for one run.

Anna M: posted dispatch log excerpt:

````
[dispatch] batch_size=16, batch_tokens=2048 -> chosen_kernel=cutlass_sgemm.large
[dispatch] local_seq_stride=128 -> heuristic_score=0.72
[dispatch] kv_prefetch_hit=false -> fallback_to_large
````

Mike L: kv_prefetch_hit=false is suspicious. We recently changed kvcache sweep to async; maybe timing of prefetch races with dispatch and batch sampler.

Lucy G: let's try two experiments:
1) reduce batch_window_ms from 2.0 -> 0.5 (should reduce packing variance)
2) force kernel selector override to prefer small tiled kernel when avg_seq_len<256

Raj P: I'll spin a canary with both toggles + nsys and perfetto. Can we add perfetto marker around kvcache ops? use `TRACE_MARKER("kv_prefetch")`.

perf-bot: New trace job queued: job_id=tr_2791234567_1. Link: https://perf.redwood/traces/tr_2791234567_1

Anna M: FYI the perfetto flame shows CPU-GPU gaps at the end of window where host queues memcpy. suspect prefetch kicks off too late.

Mike L: If host memcpy blocks dispatch, kernel then runs longer because it's fused with memcpy? need to inspect cudaMemcpyAsync timings and stream synchronization.

Lucy G: Good call. Add `--no-kv-prefetch` flag to runtime for a run; compare kv_get latencies.

Anna M: Running three runs now: baseline, --no-kv-prefetch, window=0.5ms + kernel-override. will post results within the hour.

Raj P: thanks. If the no-prefetch removes spikes, we can debounce prefetch start with 1ms lead.

Lucy G: Also consider changing kernel_cost model to penalize large cutlass when avg_seq<256.

Anna M: quick note: timeline thumbnail: https://perf.redwood/thumbs/2791234567.png :thumbsup:

Mike L: tracked UI alert: batch_window_utilization dropped by 4% with window=0.5 but p50 latency improved. tradeoff acceptable for endpoints.

Anna M: Results posted: last run with both fixes removed the 3-4ms spikes. p95 went from 18ms -> 12ms. attaching logs.

Lucy G: nice! please open a PR to default window to 0.5 for small models and add selector change. also add unit test reproducing kvcache race.

Anna M: on it. will include nsys/perfetto links and attach traces to the PR.

perf-bot: Incident note: perf-regression ticket #IN-472 created to track changes.
